_comment: ADOPT: the identity registry seam (Loom 2.0 §8) — mounted as docs/governance/identities.json, CODEOWNERS-owned by a NON-builder group. Every approver, validator and classifier field resolves against this registry: `validated_by: 'Risk'` does not pass; an identity must exist, hold the required role, and satisfy the separation rules (agents approve nothing; second-line members are not builders). Authentication of these identities (SSO/signing) is the platform's half — see attestation-issuers.template.json; this registry is the repo-side contract the gates enforce deterministically.
_roles_not_headcount: The role set is a regulatory minimum of ROLES, not an org chart. One person may hold several — eng-omar below carries `engineering` and `enterprise-architect`, the engineering manager who owns the domain's architecture alongside the product owner. Only three separations can never collapse, and the gates enforce all three: builders and second-line are disjoint; agents hold no approval role; and four-eyes needs a second human at the merge. Map the rest to as few people as your institution honestly can.
_architect_independence_residual: STATED, NOT ENFORCED: both architect roles sit in `builders` in this reference registry, because architecture is first-line design work. The consequence is that a builder-held architect can sign the architecture assurance (A1–A5) for a change they helped build, with only the four-eyes merge behind it — architecture assurance here is FIRST-line assurance, and the independent challenge comes from the second line separately. If your institution requires architecture assurance to be independent, move `enterprise-architect` to a non-builder identity and add it to the second-line role set in `product-approval-check.mjs`. The Loom does not decide this for you; it refuses to let the choice stay implicit.

groups.builders: first-line identities that author changes (humans and agents)
groups.second-line: independent risk / compliance / validation identities — MUST be disjoint from builders

identities.display: Floor projector — git read → collaboration-surface write (delete if you run no external surface)
Floor freezer — exports a collaborative draft into a branch and opens the PR; never merges
Floor bridge — TRANSCRIBES an external decision into an approval attestation. Proves custody, never authority: it may not issue the human's assertion

identities.note: WS6 D6.3 floor-keeper: prefills the non-judgment fields, converses, routes. Holds NO role and NO grant on any container carrying an approval field — core/floor-keeper.mjs refuses both. core/floor-approval-surface.mjs fixes this id as KEEPER_IDENTITY, so an adopter who renames it must change that constant too.
